chunks: And ‘Abdullāh ibn Sinān narrated from Abū ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

“You supplicate against the enemy in the Witr, and if you wish you may name them; and you seek forgiveness, and you raise your hands in the Witr level with your face, and if you wish, you open your garment.”

key_terms.الْعَدُوِّ: the enemy against whom supplication may be made
key_terms.الْوِتْرِ: the Witr prayer, specifically the context of du‘a and qunūt
key_terms.تَرْفَعُ: you raise, referring here to raising the hands
key_terms.وَجْهِكَ: your face, indicating the position of the raised hands

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام say about supplication and raising the hands in the Witr prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith describes aspects of the qunūt in the Witr prayer, including supplicating against enemies, seeking forgiveness, and raising the hands. It indicates permissibility in naming specific enemies and in how one holds or opens one's garment while making du‘a in Witr.
